newsitem.title: USA: US late spot heat gains, gasoline eases with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US late spot heat gains, gasoline eases with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. spot refined products prices were mixed late Monday, with heating oil making moderate gains and most gasoline grades easing slightly tracking February NYMEX values, players said.

Differentials on heating oil and low sulfur diesel were stable with Friday levels in both centers, although jet fuel was talked 0.75 cent higher in New York Harbor and 0.25 cent firmer in the Gulf Coast, players said.
New York Harbor heating oil was talked about 0.10 cent below February futures, or about 67.20 cents a gallon, while Gulf Coast material was offered about 3.50 cents below the print.
Conventional unleaded gasoline diffs were stable in both centers, players said, with NYH "M5-grade" talked 0.75 cent below the print, and Gulf Coast material at 1.25 cents below.
NYMEX reformulated-specification February gasoline settled 0.13 cent lower than Friday after trading in positive territory much of the day.

"Reformulated couldn't decide what to do, whether to be strong based on low stocks, or weak due to incoming cargoes and the fact that February is not traditionally a strong gasoline month," one Gulf trader said.
((- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632))
